analyst_view.overall: Early view: Game 2 in Columbus on Friday 27 November, six days after Game 1; if Miami win in Florida, Columbus must win to force a decider, and a draw goes to penalties. Columbus won eight of their last nine league games under interim coach Laurent Courtois, though Miami had gone eight regular-season meetings without losing to Columbus as of late September. This view will change a lot with the Game 1 result.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals. Both sides are scoring freely (Columbus 24 in their last nine, Miami 80 for the season) and a team behind in the series has to open up, which supports a high number; I stay close to it but would not go higher until I see how Game 1 plays out.

corners.text: The site expects 8.3 corners. I lean lower for the same reason as in Game 1: Miami build through Messi and De Paul in the middle and won only two corners against Charlotte, and Columbus took four in Chicago. A home crowd may push Columbus wider, but not by much.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. I lean a little higher: a second meeting in six days carries more edge, especially if Columbus are facing elimination at home, and Miami committed 14 fouls against Charlotte in their last game.

shots.text: The site expects 26.0 shots. Both teams have been efficient rather than shot-heavy (each took 11 shots on Decision Day and scored three or four), so I lean slightly lower, though a Columbus side chasing the series could push the count up late.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. Gonzalo Tapia and Brais Mendez have been finishing well for Columbus and Miami's attack is the league's best, so I see no reason to move away from the number.
